task_instance: Given a sample multi-entry Simplicite-style raw .txt log file (including a multi-line Java stack trace), implement and run a log-to-JSON converter script that parses timestamp/level/app/endpoint/contextPath/event/user/class/function/rowId header fields plus a multi-line body, filters output to --include timestamp,level,body, writes to an output JSON file, and prints a 'Processed: N entries, Skipped: N entries' summary to stderr; also verified default (no --include) and stdout-only modes.
evidence: Created sample_logs.txt (4 log entries, one with a 6-line Java stack trace/multiline body). Wrote simplicite-log2json.py implementing the regex-based header parser + multiline body accumulation described in SKILL.md (the skill's own /scripts/ directory was absent from the source, containing only SKILL.md and LICENSE, so the script was authored from the documented behavior/spec). Ran: `python3 simplicite-log2json.py sample_logs.txt --include timestamp,level,body --output logs_minified.json` -> exit 0, stderr printed 'Processed: 4 entries, Skipped: 0 entries', and logs_minified.json (899 bytes vs 1226-byte source) contains 4 objects each with exactly {timestamp, level, body}, with the multi-line stack trace correctly preserved inside a single 'body' string (verified via cat and by re-loading the JSON with python3 json.load). Also ran without --include to confirm all 10 documented fields (timestamp, app, level, endpoint, contextPath, event, user, class, function, rowId, body) are present in full mode, and confirmed stdout-only operation (no --output) pipes valid JSON to another process. All files are under the work directory.
